item.title: The Asymmetry of Asynchrony
item.description:
“Time is decoupled from action.”

One of my favorite programming paradigms—one that has countless analogues in our complex modern world—is asynchrony. We take it for granted that we can request a service, allow it to execute in the background, and receive what we want in a reasonable amount of time. This was one of the great transformative processes of our 21st-century world, something technologically infeasible before the rise of the telephone. Modern systems are designed to never wait.
